messages:
Sara L: FYI customer (Beacon Health) hit repeated streaming cutoffs + reconnects. They see partial JSON payloads, then client reconnects and sometimes gets the tail duplicated. Also reported a sudden billing spike for that session.

Sara L: Logs from their session:```
[stream] writev failed: EAGAIN
[stream] send: wrote 0/512
[handler] aborting stream: downstream slow consumer
http_resp: 500 on flush
trace_id=tr-9a8b7c
```

Ryan H: Can you grab the full trace_id and the request id? Any 502/503 upstreams around the same time?

Sara L: trace_id above is full. I also see this in control plane logs: `req_id=rq-1f2d3a` — first reconnect attempt returned 401 (token refresh), second succeeded with 200 but body was truncated.

Alex C: Sounds like classic slow-consumer backpressure. Kernel send buffer fills, writev returns EAGAIN, our runtime eventually aborts the stream. If the client reconnects and we resume without dedupe, they can see duplicates.

Alex C: Quick repro suggestion for eng: on a test client run `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem rate 120kbit delay 120ms` then stream a ~10s response and see server-side aborts.

Ingrid M: Ask customer for the client stack (node/python), SDK version + whether they're behind a corporate proxy. Also request a pcap or tcpdump of the session if possible. :eyes:

Sara L: Customer uses Node SDK v0.9.3, behind an enterprise proxy (BlueGate). They can share tcpdump for 1-minute window — I'm coordinating upload.

Ryan H: Two action items for runtime: (1) improve server-side handling so aborted streams emit a final error event instead of silent close (2) add a dedupe token on reconnects so resumed sessions don't replay last chunk. Filing followups with eng-runtime.

Alex C: Also can we surface keepalive and per-socket sndbuf usage in Console? That would help customers troubleshoot backpressure without dumps.

Sara L: Billing note — customer got billed for both partial + resumed responses. Support -> billing flagged as potential double-charge. I'm looping in billing.

Ingrid M: If token refresh returned 401 during reconnect, that could explain a small window where the client retries at app layer and ends up re-requesting content. Ask customer to log their retry IDs.

Ryan H: For now, workaround: bump client read buffer and enable HTTP/2 connection-level keepalive, and in Node set `socket.setKeepAlive(true, 20000)`. Also enable idempotency keys for streaming sessions so server can detect duplicates.

Sara L: I'm tagging this as P2, attaching tcpdump when available, customer is blocked on stable streaming for a pilot next week. Escalating to eng-runtime with trace_id + req_id. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2028, assigned to eng-runtime oncall. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2028

Alex C: I'll take the oncall ticket. Will try to reproduce with netem and a proxy in front. If we confirm it's slow-consumer induced, plan is: improved logging + a graceful abort event + dedupe header in short term.

Sara L: Thanks, team. I'll update customer with suggested client changes and that eng is investigating.
